rules.header_subtitle: Learn how the setup works, how turns progress, what the Executioner does, and how to win.
rules.step1_desc: Organize the play area by placing the **Black Market (BM)** deck on the left, line up the **Plot Armor (PA)** cards face up in the center by property color (Intelligence, Wisdom, Dexterity, and Strength) — note that their number equals the **total number of players**, e.g., if there are 2 players, there will be 2 Strength PAs, 2 Intelligence PAs, 2 Dexterity PAs, and 2 Wisdom PAs — and place the Executioner deck on the far right.
rules.step2_title: Step 2: Creation of the Death Line
rules.step2_desc: Right below the top row, set up the **Death Line** by placing the Main Deck (MD) at the far right end. The significance of the Death Line is crucial, as whoever remains alive until the end wins:
rules.step2_list1: The Executioner: Always takes the very first position at the far left end.
rules.step2_list2: The Peasants: Place all Peasant cards immediately after the Executioner. They act as a protective buffer before any player is in danger.
rules.step2_list3: Character Selection: All players choose a character to represent them for the game. Shuffle the chosen Character cards and pick one at random to decide who goes first in line behind the Peasants.
rules.step2_list4: Seating Arrangement: Place the remaining player characters in order, following the natural seating order around the table, clockwise. At the start of the game, each player gets 3 cards in hand from the Main Deck (MD).
rules.step3_desc: Right below the Death Line, create the Board by drawing cards from the Main Deck (MD).
rules.step3_list1: Number of Board Cards: Deal a number of cards equal to the number of players + 2 to the board.
rules.step3_list2: Card Types: The board contains cards where Resource cards are face up, while Action cards are face down.
rules.adjustments_title: Deck Adjustments Based on Player Count
rules.adjustments_desc: Depending on how many players are participating, you may need to adjust the Main Deck (MD) to keep the game balanced. With 3 or 4 players, use the full deck as per normal.
rules.adjustments_2p_intro: If you are playing with only 2 players, remove the following cards from the central deck before starting:
rules.phase1_desc: The game officially begins with the Draw Phase, the first of the three phases of each round.
rules.phase1_list1: Play Order: Players play strictly in the order they are positioned on the Death Line.
rules.phase1_list2: Card Selection: The first character in line chooses and draws one card of their choice directly from the available cards on the Board.
rules.phase1_list3: Empty Board Rule: If there are no available cards on the board when your turn comes, draw your card directly from the Main Deck (MD).
rules.phase1_complete_desc: Drawing continues along the line until every player has chosen one card from the board.
rules.phase1_complete_list1: Turn Sequence: After the first player, the next player in line takes their card, and so on.
rules.phase1_complete_list2: Board Shrinking: As players take cards, the board will naturally shrink. Once all players have drawn one card, the Draw Phase ends.
rules.phase2_desc1: Once all players have drawn one card, the Action Phase begins according to the queue order, starting with the first player on the Death Line.
rules.phase2_desc2: On your turn, you can perform one of the following three main options:
rules.phase2_opt1: 1) Play an Action Card: Play a blue action card from your hand into your play area, immediately apply its effect, and then send it to the discard pile.
rules.phase2_opt2: 2) Buy a Plot Armor Card: Discard 3 identical Resource cards + 1 Holy Duck Tape card from your hand to acquire the corresponding Plot Armor card. Note: The Plot Armor card does NOT go to the discard pile when you use its effect, it stays in front of you and you can use it once per round.
rules.phase2_opt2_ex: Example: Discarding 3 Wisdom resources and one Holy Duck Tape wins you a Wisdom Plot Armor card.
rules.phase2_opt3: 3) Buy or Play a Black Market Card: Discard any 3 cards from your hand to take the top card from the Black Market deck.
rules.phase2_priority_title: Priority & Passing in the Action Phase
rules.phase2_priority_text1: During the Action Phase, each player takes one action on their turn, or may choose to pass and do nothing.
rules.phase2_priority_text2: The Action Phase ends only when all players pass consecutively one after the other.
rules.phase2_ex1_title: Example of Playing an Action Card
rules.phase2_ex1_text: The active player plays Unfair Trade to immediately execute its effect ("Draw 2 cards from the Main Deck"). Right after, the card goes to the discard pile as shown in the image below.
rules.phase2_ex2_text: To buy a Strength Plot Armor card, surrender 3 Strength cards along with 1 Holy Duck Tape card.
rules.phase3_desc: When all players have passed, reveal the top card of the Executioner Deck. (Note: When the Executioner's cards run out, shuffle them to seamlessly continue Phase 3).
rules.phase3_list1: Board Refresh: When the board needs refreshing, existing cards are not burned, but empty slots are filled with cards from the Main Deck (MD) by dealing a number of cards equal to the number of players + 2.
rules.phase3_list2: "YOU ARE UP NEXT": When this card is revealed, the Executioner executes the very next target in line on the Death Line.
rules.phase3_list3: Peasant Protection: The Executioner must execute all 3 Peasants first before any player character is in danger.
rules.phase3_list4: Flipping to Death State: When a player character dies, flip their card over to reveal the Death State artwork and the player is removed from the game.
rules.phase3_ex1_text: By drawing "YOU ARE UP NEXT", the Executioner moves forward and executes the next target in line.
rules.phase3_ex2_text: Characters that are executed flip over to reveal their Death State.
rules.purpose_text1: Prove that you are the protagonist! The first player to collect 3 Plot Armor cards wins.
rules.purpose_text2: Alternatively, if all other players die, the last survivor wins immediately.

executioner.name: The Executioner
executioner.description: Beauty is both a blessing and a curse. That's the problem of our beloved Executioner. Legends say his first conquest was the midwife who delivered him. Having spent his entire life as the embodiment of the halo effect, he grew tired. What's the point when everything and everyone comes so easily? So, he did the only thing that made sense: he decided he is a fighter, not a lover. He took over the family business and became the new Executioner. Associated with death itself, surely people would stop looking at him just for his looks. And with endless grace and sex appeal, even in this, he finally succeeded. Now he is not just a handsome guy. He is the sexy Executioner.

notferatu.name: Notferatu
notferatu.description: He is a ruthless and relentless vampire hunter. After his mother died when a vampire that cursed her blood (-she suffered form sepsis), he vowed to dedicate his life to becoming the greatest vampire hunter in the world, so no one else would ever go through what he did. After years of training and finding the perfect equipment, he is finally ready to face a vampire... once he finds one. His latest trick? Dressing up as a vampire himself so that a real one would come out of hiding without fear... and then... then... the local villagers mistook him for a vampire and sent him to be executed. He is now waving garlic around, scubbbing off his makeup, and shouting that he is a human hoping to saved himself. En vain, though, since everyone already knows he is human, they just wanted an excuse to get rid of him after 10 long years driving everyone crazy with his vampire obsession.

misero.name: Misero
misero.description: Humor ages with man. We don't know if that's true, but that is the state of the king's once-beloved clown. After more than 40 years of jokes, cream pies and sarcasm, this clown stopped spreading smiles and joy. In a last attempt to become funny again, he decided to reinvent himself by changing his stage name from Bozo to Smiley, Harley King, Sad Sad Sammy, and every other terrible name imaginable, until he finally gave up and called himself Misero. Now, all he wants is to retire. But the king won't let him because, besides being useless enterntainment, he also happen to be the king's only real advisor (when you're the clown who no one pays attention to, you over hear a lot). Finally, he decided to go out the way he lived: with a joke. He made a particularly vulgar one about the queen's behind and ended up in line for execution. He is oddly happy about it, until a child gives him a clown scepter and says he is his biggest fan. Realizing he can still make someone laugh, Misero decides... it's not his time yet.

paprika.name: Paprika
paprika.description: A young maid with a talent for cooking who, despite being barely able to read, finds a spice book with pictures and uses it for her next pie. She leaves everyone speechless as they've just tasted the most gourmet medieval dish imaginable. A woman who's good at something, can read, and uses spices? She must be a witch! The court sentenced her to two months of community service, but she requested execution because she is in love with the Executioner (she thinks she can "fix" him). After annoying the judge for over 3 hours, he gave up and sentenced her to death. Unfortunately, while waiting in the execution line, she suddenly remembered that if the Executioner kills her, she will never see him again! So, she decided to escape and change her approach.

hamlet.name: Hamlet
hamlet.description: It's the Middle Ages. A pig appears out of nowhere, knocks a flowerpot off a lady's balcony, and it falls on the head of the local lord, killing him instantly. Would you call that man slaughter or murder? Whether it's a pig doesn't matter... someone must pay for this tragic accident. The worst part? The pig actually is intelligent and self aware. In fact, he is a secret member and informant of an underground organization plotting against the regime. His plan all along was to assassinate the noble so that the city would fall into the control of this secret order and all without breaking the law! After all, who would accuse a pig? Well, everyone actually, because he forgot he's in the Middle Ages when people do believe animals have consciousness and criminal law is still in its early stage and so a cunning conspirator now finds himself desperately trying not to become bacon.
